findings.summary: After BF16 embeddings, OCR takes 84.6% of the measured NACA call. Scheduling is the next target.
observations: Median NACA call: 3.95 s; OCR 3.33 s; embedding 0.48 s.
One warm-up and three ordinary measurements are separate from the bounded engine trace. The instrumented full output passes the original frozen reference.
The four recognizers retain their server limit of four running regions. Current requests are submitted in groups of sixteen per page worker.
The earlier Census study showed a late page-5 sequence and three mostly idle GPUs. Embedding precision leaves that OCR scheduling problem unchanged.
GPU activity and request counts describe usage; they do not establish percentage of peak compute or bandwidth.

During measured NACA OCR, each server reached its four-request limit; waiting-request gauges peaked at 7–8 and were nonzero in 22%–28% of OCR-window samples. Test a higher server batch limit after the client/page scheduling sweep.
findings.next_step: Test a wider region submission window and dynamic page assignment as separate changes.
findings.optimization: Keep BF16/16-chunk embedding and all OCR semantics fixed; compare window 64 and next-free-worker page scheduling against a fresh control.
